title: Minimum Covering Window
statement:
Find the shortest piece of a text that contains every character of a required text, counting repeats.

Contract
- `source` and `required` are non-null and contain only ASCII characters (code below 128); matching is case-sensitive.
- A window is a contiguous substring of `source`. It qualifies when, for every character, it holds at least as many copies as `required` does (so `"LLO"` needs two `L`).
- Return the shortest qualifying window. If several have the same shortest length, return the leftmost.
- Return `""` if no window qualifies or if `required` is empty.

Examples
- `minimumWindow("HELLOWORLD", "LLO")` returns `"LLO"`.
- `minimumWindow("abc", "d")` returns `""`.
- `minimumWindow("a", "a")` returns `"a"`.
hints: Count how many copies of each character are required. A window qualifies when none of those counts is still short.
Expand the right end until the window qualifies, then move the left end forward for as long as it still qualifies, recording the shortest window seen.

Track the number of characters still missing instead of rescanning counts, and keep a window only when strictly shorter so the leftmost wins. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space (a fixed ASCII table), where n is the source length with the required text treated as a small constant.
inputSyntax: Input: the source and required text, each in single quotes, for example: 'HELLOWORLD' 'LLO'
